title: Quran, Sura 69 (al-ḥāqqah) (Codex Parisino-petropolitanus)
source: Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (BnF Arabe 328) via Gallica IIIF + Corpus Coranicum folio mapping + Tanzil + Pickthall
description: Sura 69 (al-ḥāqqah) from the Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (c. 650-750 AD), one section per folio side, each linked to the exact Gallica image of that page (2 pages).
introduction:
Sura 69 (al-ḥāqqah) as preserved on 2 folio sides of the Codex Parisino-petropolitanus (Paris, BnF Arabe 328 (a) and (b)), one of the oldest surviving Quran manuscripts, written in hijazi script on parchment, c. 650-750 AD. Each section below is one folio side, and the image shown is that exact page.

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side from Gallica (Bibliotheque nationale de France IIIF). The folio's sura:verse range was taken from the Corpus Coranicum "Manuscripta Coranica" record for that page, which states the first and last word on the page; the folio numbers of both services were cross-checked by comparing the two images pixel by pixel.
  2. Original text: the Arabic of the Tanzil Project Uthmani text (CC BY 3.0), reproduced unchanged, verse by verse.
  3. English: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), public domain, verse by verse.

Orthography: the codex is written in scriptio defectiva: no vowel signs, almost no consonantal dots, long vowels often unwritten, and letter shapes that differ from the printed Uthmani text. The modern text given here therefore differs orthographically from what is on the folio while conveying the same reading; readers should expect, for example, the basmala and words such as qala to be spelled with fewer letters on the page.

Numbering: verse numbers follow the standard Kufan (Cairo 1924) division used by Corpus Coranicum, Tanzil and Pickthall. Early codices mark verse ends with ink dots that in places divide the text differently, so a verse count made on the page may not match these numbers exactly. In Tanzil's text the basmala opening each sura (except sura 9) is printed as part of verse 1. Where a page begins or ends in the middle of a verse the whole verse is given and the word position is stated in the section heading.

Lacunae: the surviving Paris leaves do not carry every verse of this sura. Only the verses listed in the sections below are on the folios shown; the rest of the sura is lost or preserved in other fragments of the same codex (St Petersburg Marcel 18, Vatican Ar. 1605/1, London KFQ 60) that are not included here.
translator_notes: 50 of 52 verses of this sura survive on the Paris leaves of the codex (2 folio sides).
Corpus Coranicum records the first and last word of each page; a verse split across two pages is shown in full under both pages with the word position noted.

translation.original_ref: Quran 69:3-35, BnF Arabe 328 fol. 69r (page ends at word 5 of 69:35)
translation.original_text: <sup>3</sup>وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلْحَآقَّةُ <sup>4</sup>كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وَعَادٌۢ بِٱلْقَارِعَةِ <sup>5</sup>فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ بِٱلطَّاغِيَةِ <sup>6</sup>وَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ <sup>7</sup>سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا فَتَرَى ٱلْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ <sup>8</sup>فَهَلْ تَرَىٰ لَهُم مِّنۢ بَاقِيَةٍ <sup>9</sup>وَجَآءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَن قَبْلَهُۥ وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَٰتُ بِٱلْخَاطِئَةِ <sup>10</sup>فَعَصَوْا۟ رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةً رَّابِيَةً <sup>11</sup>إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا ٱلْمَآءُ حَمَلْنَٰكُمْ فِى ٱلْجَارِيَةِ <sup>12</sup>لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنٌ وَٰعِيَةٌ <sup>13</sup>فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ وَٰحِدَةٌ <sup>14</sup>وَحُمِلَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَٰحِدَةً <sup>15</sup>فَيَوْمَئِذٍ وَقَعَتِ ٱلْوَاقِعَةُ <sup>16</sup>وَٱنشَقَّتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَهِىَ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاهِيَةٌ <sup>17</sup>وَٱلْمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرْجَآئِهَا وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمَٰنِيَةٌ <sup>18</sup>يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ <sup>19</sup>فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ هَآؤُمُ ٱقْرَءُوا۟ كِتَٰبِيَهْ <sup>20</sup>إِنِّى ظَنَنتُ أَنِّى مُلَٰقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ <sup>21</sup>فَهُوَ فِى عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ <sup>22</sup>فِى جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ <sup>23</sup>قُطُوفُهَا دَانِيَةٌ <sup>24</sup>كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ هَنِيٓـًٔۢا بِمَآ أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِى ٱلْأَيَّامِ ٱلْخَالِيَةِ <sup>25</sup>وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِشِمَالِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيْتَنِى لَمْ أُوتَ كِتَٰبِيَهْ <sup>26</sup>وَلَمْ أَدْرِ مَا حِسَابِيَهْ <sup>27</sup>يَٰلَيْتَهَا كَانَتِ ٱلْقَاضِيَةَ <sup>28</sup>مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّى مَالِيَهْ <sup>29</sup>هَلَكَ عَنِّى سُلْطَٰنِيَهْ <sup>30</sup>خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ <sup>31</sup>ثُمَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ <sup>32</sup>ثُمَّ فِى سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًا فَٱسْلُكُوهُ <sup>33</sup>إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ <sup>34</sup>وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ <sup>35</sup>فَلَيْسَ لَهُ ٱلْيَوْمَ هَٰهُنَا حَمِيمٌ
translation.text: <sup>3</sup>Ah, what will convey unto thee what the reality is! <sup>4</sup>(The tribes of) Thamud and A'ad disbelieved in the judgment to come. <sup>5</sup>As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the lightning. <sup>6</sup>And as for A'ad, they were destroyed by a fierce roaring wind, <sup>7</sup>Which He imposed on them for seven long nights and eight long days so that thou mightest have seen men lying overthrown, as they were hollow trunks of palm-trees. <sup>8</sup>Canst thou (O Muhammad) see any remnant of them? <sup>9</sup>And Pharaoh and those before him, and the communities that were destroyed, brought error, <sup>10</sup>And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, therefor did He grip them with a tightening grip. <sup>11</sup>Lo! when the waters rose, We carried you upon the ship <sup>12</sup>That We might make it a memorial for you, and that remembering ears (that heard the story) might remember. <sup>13</sup>And when the trumpet shall sound one blast <sup>14</sup>And the earth with the mountains shall be lifted up and crushed with one crash, <sup>15</sup>Then, on that day will the Event befall. <sup>16</sup>And the heaven will split asunder, for that day it will be frail. <sup>17</sup>And the angels will be on the sides thereof, and eight will uphold the Throne of thy Lord that day, above them. <sup>18</sup>On that day ye will be exposed; not a secret of you will be hidden. <sup>19</sup>Then, as for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: Take, read my book! <sup>20</sup>Surely I knew that I should have to meet my reckoning. <sup>21</sup>Then he will be in blissful state <sup>22</sup>In a high garden <sup>23</sup>Whereof the clusters are in easy reach. <sup>24</sup>(And it will be said unto those therein): Eat and drink at ease for that which ye sent on before you in past days. <sup>25</sup>But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: Oh, would that I had not been given my book <sup>26</sup>And knew not what my reckoning! <sup>27</sup>Oh, would that it had been death! <sup>28</sup>My wealth hath not availed me, <sup>29</sup>My power hath gone from me. <sup>30</sup>(It will be said): Take him and fetter him <sup>31</sup>And then expose him to hell-fire <sup>32</sup>And then insert him in a chain whereof the length is seventy cubits. <sup>33</sup>Lo! He used not to believe in Allah the Tremendous, <sup>34</sup>And urged not on the feeding of the wretched. <sup>35</sup>Therefor hath he no lover here this day,

translation.original_ref: Quran 69:36-52, BnF Arabe 328 fol. 69v (page begins at word 3 of 69:36; page continues into sura 70 (70:28))
translation.original_text: <sup>36</sup>وَلَا طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ <sup>37</sup>لَّا يَأْكُلُهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱلْخَٰطِـُٔونَ <sup>38</sup>فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ <sup>39</sup>وَمَا لَا تُبْصِرُونَ <sup>40</sup>إِنَّهُۥ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ <sup>41</sup>وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا مَّا تُؤْمِنُونَ <sup>42</sup>وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ <sup>43</sup>تَنزِيلٌ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ <sup>44</sup>وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ ٱلْأَقَاوِيلِ <sup>45</sup>لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِٱلْيَمِينِ <sup>46</sup>ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنَا مِنْهُ ٱلْوَتِينَ <sup>47</sup>فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَٰجِزِينَ <sup>48</sup>وَإِنَّهُۥ لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ <sup>49</sup>وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنكُم مُّكَذِّبِينَ <sup>50</sup>وَإِنَّهُۥ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ <sup>51</sup>وَإِنَّهُۥ لَحَقُّ ٱلْيَقِينِ <sup>52</sup>فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
translation.text: <sup>36</sup>Nor any food save filth <sup>37</sup>Which none but sinners eat. <sup>38</sup>But nay! I swear by all that ye see <sup>39</sup>And all that ye see not <sup>40</sup>That it is indeed the speech of an illustrious messenger. <sup>41</sup>It is not poet's speech - little is it that ye believe! <sup>42</sup>Nor diviner's speech - little is it that ye remember! <sup>43</sup>It is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds. <sup>44</sup>And if he had invented false sayings concerning Us, <sup>45</sup>We assuredly had taken him by the right hand <sup>46</sup>And then severed his life-artery, <sup>47</sup>And not one of you could have held Us off from him. <sup>48</sup>And lo! it is a warrant unto those who ward off (evil). <sup>49</sup>And lo! We know that some among you will deny (it). <sup>50</sup>And lo! it is indeed an anguish for the disbelievers. <sup>51</sup>And lo! it is absolute truth. <sup>52</sup>So glorify the name of thy Tremendous Lord.
